title: Chapter 298: Videotape
html:
Chen Ge’s bluntness caught the woman completely off guard.

“Are you a ghost?” he repeated in the casual tone of someone asking a friend whether she had eaten dinner.

The woman’s breathing quickened with unmistakable agitation. Static crackled across the line as the signal abruptly deteriorated.

“I’ll take that as a silent admission.” Chen Ge leaned against the door with his phone on his ear. He looked like he was chatting with an old friend.

“I…” She began to answer, then stopped. Somehow, Chen Ge had managed to make a ghost uncomfortable.Shouldn’t a person scream and drop the phone upon realizing they’re speaking to a ghost?

Even if he doesn’t scream, shouldn’t he at least hang up with trembling hands? Why is he asking questions instead?

The call was abruptly ended.

The dial tone did not surprise Chen Ge. Exposing her lie must have embarrassed her.

He pocketed the phone and stood in the dark corridor. Three tenants met tragic ends in Room 304. I’ve encountered the gambler and the agent, so the woman on the phone is probably the second tenant—the English teacher.

It was not yet midnight, and Chen Ge had already met three different ghosts. He felt this was only the beginning.

I wonder what kind of weird creature I’ll meet after midnight. Looks like I need to be prepared.

Chen Ge grabbed his backpack and headed for Room 304.

Instead of waiting for them to come to me, I should be more active.

Light from Room 305 spilled into the corridor. Throughout the Third Hospital Staff Residence, Chen Ge’s apartment appeared to be the only one illuminated.

Most of the tenants live in the two buildings in front. Looks like this block is a no-go zone for them.

Chen Ge tested Room 304’s lock. It broke after two hard shakes. The police had probably forced the door repeatedly during investigations, leaving obvious signs of tampering around the mechanism.

Breaking down the door is too rude and not something I like to do, but there’s no better option now.

Chen Ge made his aim and swung at the door.

Bang! Bang!

After several blows, the lock surrendered. Chen Ge wedged the hammer’s handle into the narrow opening and pried the door wide. No one investigated despite all that noise. The ghosts here must have thoroughly intimidated the neighbors.

The living-room light revealed Room 304’s peculiar condition. Its sofa and dining table appeared ordinary, but every cabinet, wardrobe, and drawer had been nailed shut with wooden planks.

Now this looks like a haunted house.

Old wiring made the light flicker incessantly, deepening the room’s unease.

Standing in the room’s center, Chen Ge ran a hand across the sofa’s back. Despite years of vacancy, it bore no dust, as though someone cleaned the apartment every day.

Two bedrooms and one living room. The layout is similar to Room 305, but the stuff is much older.

Chen Ge walked to the shoe rack. Looking at the nails on the boards, he was curious. Why are all the racks and drawers sealed? Are they hiding something scary?

One swing of the hammer opened the shoe cabinet. Several unremarkable pairs waited inside. Did these belong to the victims?

Slippers, high heels, and boots had been crammed together. As Chen Ge tossed them out, he discovered that a knife had slashed through every pair. Who did this, and why?

Chen Ge could not find anything on the shoes, so he looked elsewhere. The living room was small, and across from the sofa was a television cabinet. Interestingly enough, even the drawers under the television were sealed up by planks.

The thing that I won is called the Drawer That Cannot Be Opened. Does this mean, after I try all the drawers, the one that cannot be opened is mine?

With no one to answer him, he could only test the theory. The television cabinet’s position made removing its planks awkward, but he eventually pried them free.

He pulled open the drawer, and videotapes that were kept inside black boxes fell out.

Videotapes? How old are these?

He selected a comparatively new tape and inserted it into the VCR beneath the television. After connecting the power and switching it on, a shadow flashed across the screen.

Was that a shadow? Something just ran past me?Chen Ge stayed on high alert. He knew the gambler who had lost his left hand had run into Room 304, and he was hiding in one of the corners.

Age had degraded the recording, while static and rolling lines plagued the old television. The fact that either device still worked was miraculous. Ignoring the distortion, Chen Ge crouched before the screen.

The video showed the apartment from a fixed angle, suggesting that someone had mounted the camera in one corner.

What is he trying to record?

After a minute without movement, Chen Ge grew impatient and fast-forwarded. The recording’s first half was ordinary; the latter half was not.

The second half had been recorded at night and closely resembled Chen Ge’s present surroundings. From atop the television, the camera captured the illuminated living room and both bedroom doors.

The whole drawer is filled with videotapes, meaning the person recording them has been recording this home for a long time already.

The recorder’s purpose seemed obvious. After experiencing something supernatural, the tenant had installed a camera to capture proof.

Didn’t he know curiosity kills? He should have moved out the moment he sensed something wrong.

Chen Ge hugged the recorder to his chest and continued watching the video.

Near the end of the badly degraded recording, the previously static image abruptly changed.

The recorded lights began flickering just like those around him. With every pulse of darkness, the closed bedroom door in the video opened a little farther.
